correctness.summary: The node-merge step is a no-op, so vertices are never contracted; the global min-cut value is computed wrong for essentially any graph with n>=3.
correctness.triggeringInput: n=3 triangle with unit weights: edges (0,1),(1,2),(2,0) each weight 1. Correct min cut = 2; this returns a wrong value because phases never contract s,t and the maximum-adjacency ordering never restarts on a contracted graph.
correctness.rootCause: MergeNodes calls UpdateWeightsAfterPhase with add==null, and UpdateWeightsAfterPhase guards its only effect with `add != null`, so NO edge weights are ever merged from t into s. Furthermore merged nodes are marked vis[t]=-2, but FindMaxDistNode selects nodes with `vis[i] < phase`; since -2 < phase for all later phases, already-merged nodes are re-selected, so the contraction never takes effect. The Stoer-Wagner contraction is entirely missing.
correctness.suggestedFix: Implement real contraction: after each phase merge t into s by, for every edge incident to t, adding weight[e] to the corresponding s-incident edge (building/maintaining an adjacency-weight matrix), permanently remove t, and reset the per-phase `vis`/`dist` state so each phase runs maximum-adjacency ordering over only the still-active (non-merged) vertices. Use a dedicated 'removed' marker distinct from the per-phase visited marker.

correctness.summary: Cost transformation `maxVal - maxCost[i*n+j]` and final `(long)n * maxVal - result` can overflow Int64 for valid large long inputs, and `maxVal - minCost` overflows when costs straddle a huge range.
correctness.triggeringInput: n=2 with cost matrix containing maxVal = long.MaxValue and another entry = long.MinValue: `maxVal - cost = long.MaxValue - long.MinValue` overflows long, producing a negative weight and a wrong assignment.
correctness.rootCause: The min-to-max reduction subtracts each cost from maxVal without any range guard; differences can exceed long.MaxValue. Also `(long)n * maxVal` overflows when maxVal is near long.MaxValue.
correctness.suggestedFix: Document a bounded input range, or perform the negation/transform in a wider domain (e.g. Int128) or by negating costs (cost -> -cost) and running the min solver directly instead of the maxVal-subtraction trick.

perf.summary: Hardcoded `stackalloc int[20000]` for flow plus a full O(20000) zeroing every outer iteration, independent of actual edge count.
perf.currentCost: `int* flow = stackalloc int[20000]` is 80 KB of stack (risks stack overflow under Burst, and blows L1). The reset `for j in 0..20000: flow[j]=0` runs n-1 times = O(20000*n) writes regardless of real m. Also `bool* vis = stackalloc bool[n]` is allocated inside the loop (stackalloc in a loop does not free per iteration in C#, so this leaks stack frame space up to n*n bytes).
perf.proposedChange: Size flow by the real edge count (pass m or 2*m+2) instead of 20000; reset only the used entries. Hoist `bool* vis = stackalloc bool[n]` out of the for loop to a single allocation. Zero only `flow[1..edgeCount]`.
perf.rationale: Cuts stack footprint from fixed 80 KB to O(edges), removes O(20000*n) redundant zeroing, and stops the in-loop stackalloc from accumulating. Big cache and cycle win, and removes a Burst stack-overflow hazard on mobile.
perf.risk: Need the true edge-array length threaded into the signature (currently absent). Hoisting vis is safe because Bfs reinitializes vis[i]=false at its start. Behavior identical for valid inputs.

perf.summary: Hardcoded `stackalloc int[20000]` for the DFS stack regardless of graph size.
perf.currentCost: 80 KB fixed stack allocation; on a small graph this is wasted, on a large one (edges > ~20000) it silently overflows. Burst on mobile has tight stack budgets.
perf.proposedChange: Size the stack by the actual upper bound: the Euler circuit visits each edge once, so stack depth is bounded by (number of edges + 1). Thread the edge count in and use `stackalloc int[edgeCount + 1]`.
perf.rationale: Right-sizes stack to the problem, eliminating both waste and overflow risk; tighter working set improves cache behavior.
perf.risk: Requires an edge-count parameter. The circuit buffer is caller-allocated already, so this only affects the internal stack. Semantics unchanged.

perf.summary: Blossom contraction relabels bases with a full O(n) scan per shrink step, inflating Contract to O(n^2) per blossom.
perf.currentCost: `for i in 0..n: if base_[i]==oldBaseU || base_[i]==oldBaseMv base_[i]=lca` runs inside the while-walk up the blossom, so a single Contract is O(blossomLen * n).
perf.proposedChange: Defer base reassignment: collect the vertices on the blossom path and relabel them in one pass after the walk, or use a union-find over bases so base lookups stay near-O(1) and the explicit relabel scan disappears.
perf.rationale: Removes the nested O(n) scan from each contraction step; brings blossom matching closer to its standard O(V^3) (or better) bound instead of an inflated constant.
perf.risk: Must keep base_ semantics consistent for the subsequent GetLca/relax logic. Union-find variant changes how base_ is read everywhere; the deferred single-pass relabel is the lower-risk option. Verify against matching tests.

perf.summary: Allocates an n*n scratch matrix to hold the negated cost, doubling the working set for a pure transform.
perf.currentCost: `long* maxCost = stackalloc long[n*n]` is 8*n^2 bytes of stack on top of the caller's cost matrix; for n in the hundreds this is large stack pressure and a full O(n^2) copy.
perf.proposedChange: Two options: (a) require the caller to pass scratch, or (b) since HungarianMin only reads cost[(i)*n+j], pass a small bias (maxVal) and a flag so HungarianMin computes (maxVal - cost) on the fly, avoiding the materialized matrix entirely. At minimum fuse the two loops (find maxVal and copy) — currently maxVal is found in the same double loop, then a second full O(n^2) pass negates; the negation pass cannot start until maxVal is known, but the initial copy is redundant since you could store cost directly and subtract in the second pass reading original cost.
perf.rationale: Eliminates an 8*n^2-byte stack buffer and one O(n^2) copy pass; reduces cache footprint for the subsequent Hungarian solve.
perf.risk: On-the-fly negation requires threading a transform into HungarianMin (API change). The fuse-only variant is safe and behavior-preserving. Result formula `(long)n*maxVal - result` unchanged.

perf.summary: Preference-rank inverse table is indexed with `w*n + mID`; multiply per access can be strength-reduced, and the two classes are byte-identical duplicates.
perf.currentCost: Every womanRank/receiverRank access recomputes `idx*n + other` (a multiply) in hot proposal loops. Two near-identical implementations also double code size / icache.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist row-base pointers (`long* row = womanRank + w*n`) outside inner loops where w is fixed, turning index math into a single add. Collapse GaleShapley to delegate to StableMarriage (the proposerIsMan flag is unused in the body) to remove duplicate code.
perf.rationale: Removes a multiply from the per-access address computation in the rank-table build loops and reduces instruction-cache duplication.
perf.risk: Ergonomics/icache only; outputs identical. Confirm proposerIsMan truly has no behavioral effect before collapsing (it is written nowhere in the shown body).

perf.summary: MergeNodes calls UpdateWeightsAfterPhase with add=null (a no-op guarded by `add != null`), so the merge does no weight folding — flag as dead/incorrect code rather than optimize.
perf.currentCost: UpdateWeightsAfterPhase's body `if (vis[to[e]]==phase && add != null) add[last]+=...` can never execute since add is always null here; the call is pure overhead and the intended merge bookkeeping is missing.
perf.proposedChange: Remove the dead call or implement the real Stoer-Wagner merge (fold t's incident weights into s). As-is the routine likely produces wrong min-cuts; do not micro-optimize until the algorithm is corrected.
perf.rationale: Eliminating provably-dead branches removes wasted edge-scan cycles; correcting the merge is required for the result to be meaningful.
perf.risk: This is a correctness flag, not a semantics-preserving micro-opt. Verify intended behavior against tests before changing; reported here so the dead branch isn't mistaken for live hot code.
